name: Süreklilik, varlıklar ve deneyim motoru
what_this_proves: This system starts learning from what it did. The Experience Engine has been complete since it was written and the only thing that ever called it was a manual POST: the feature matrix measured the result exactly, 1441 activity events and 0 memories. A system that keeps a durable record of everything it does and never reads it back is keeping a diary it cannot remember.
the_shape_of_this_batch: Four complete mechanisms, none of which had a caller - the fifth batch in a row where the dominant defect is not broken code but finished code nobody reaches. The Experience Engine (a manual POST), the entity graph (`Entity`, `EntityEdge`, eight kinds, service functions and a REST surface, zero callers in `app/`), and two link columns in the memory schema (`project_id`, `conversation_id`) that `RetrievalFilters` can already scope by and `hybrid_search` already scores - and that nothing ever filled. A link column nothing fills is a join nobody can make.

closed_fully.71_the_engine_gets_a_clock: It rides the routine clock and throttles itself to its own interval, which is the Evolution Supervisor's own pattern - one cadence in this process rather than a timer per subsystem. Last in the tick order, behind the evolution scan and for the same reason: it reads the ledger and writes memories, which is the slowest thing on a clock that also fires alarms, and the least urgent.
closed_fully.71_it_walks_TWO_directions_and_that_is_t: `ledger.query` is newest-first and capped at 200 rows. A scheduler that only asks for "everything since my last pass" keeps up with today and never reaches the 1441 events that were already there; one that only asks for the newest page re-reads it for ever. So a pass does both: catch up forward, then - if there is room left in the page budget - walk one page further back. The backlog finishes when a backward page comes back short.
closed_fully.71_the_cursor_is_a_ledger_event: Each pass writes `experience.ingested` carrying the window it scanned, and the next pass reads the latest one. Three reasons rather than a table: "when did the engine last run and how far back has it read" becomes answerable through `activity.explain` like everything else; there is no private state to disagree with the memories actually written; and a cursor derived from the memories WOULD STALL, because an event whose summary the write policy ignores produces no row and a whole page of those would leave it where it started.
closed_fully.47_the_graph_gets_a_producer: Built only from what the ledger already carries as identity - the subsystem that acted, the action it performed, the research job or goal it was working on. Nothing parses a sentence. There are no `person` nodes and that is the honest answer rather than a gap: no field in the ledger names a person, and a graph of guesses is exactly what this product's write policy exists to refuse.
closed_fully.48_identity_was_already_device_independe: Satisfied by the identity SCHEME, not by anything built here: `Entity` is unique on `(kind, name)` and carries no device column, so the same logical subsystem observed through two different sources is one node. True since the table was written and untestable while nothing wrote to it; with a producer, a test can say so.
closed_fully.46_50_the_two_link_columns: A memory taught by voice now records the conversation that taught it and the project the owner opened DURING that conversation. `Memory.conversation_id` makes "you told me this while we were talking about X" answerable at all; `Memory.project_id` makes what was learned while working on something findable from that something later, across sessions.

corrected_by_measurement.49_the_focus_mechanism_has_existed_since: Recorded 'Yok | MISSING'. `app/operator/focus.py` has provided `current`/`previous`/`stack` per kind since M19, with 15 kinds, append-only with recency ordering, and its own docstring says it exists so a deictic word ("bunu kapat", "öndeki pencere") can be resolved. Eight packages use it and `previous()` alone has eight call sites. What was genuinely missing was a `memory` kind - so B18 added one and `memory.search` now focuses what it reads aloud. Fourth measurement correction in five batches, and the largest: the matrix was describing production ROWS, not code.
corrected_by_measurement.48_the_same: 'Yazılı, kullanılmıyor' was right about the second half and wrong about what remained: nothing needed writing, only a producer for the graph so the property could be exercised.

found_on_the_way.the_graph_built_a_graph_of_itself_buildi: The first draft did not apply the engine's exclusion list to the graph's own read, so a pass read this pass's `experience.ingested` receipt and grew a `system: memory` node and a `capability: experience.ingest` node - one more of each, every pass, for ever. Caught by `test_a_second_pass_adds_no_duplicate_nodes_or_edges`, which is precisely the shape that finds it. The exclusion list is now public and both writers share it: one list, applied once.
found_on_the_way.a_project_focus_that_never_expires: `focus.current` has no staleness bound, which is correct for its original users - a deictic word means the most recent thing, however long ago. It is wrong for a DURABLE link stamped on every memory taught afterwards: a project opened once in March would be attached to a preference taught in June, and a join that is always true is not a join. The link is bounded to the project opened during THIS conversation, compared against the realtime session's own `created_at`, which needs no arbitrary window.
found_on_the_way.a_swallowed_exception_poisoned_the_sessi: The focus write's best-effort catch had no `session.rollback()`, so a failed flush left the session in `PendingRollbackError` and the next statement failed somewhere the owner could not connect to it. Written correctly three times today in other modules and missed here; the test surfaced it immediately. Also reordered: the focus write happens BEFORE the use receipts, because `set_focus` commits and a failure inside it rolls back - the cheaper thing should be the one that can be lost.
found_on_the_way.the_backlog_cursor_seeded_from_the_wrong: First draft seeded the backward walk from `since` - which on a first run is "24 hours ago" - so with a fixture whose history was hours old the backward window asked for events older than that, found none, and declared the backlog finished having read four of twelve events. A cursor seeded from a horizon rather than from data is always wrong in whichever direction the data is not.

honest_about_the_counts: `events_scanned` is rows READ, not distinct events: the backlog half starts at the forward half's oldest row and `until` is inclusive, so that one row is read twice on purpose. An exclusive boundary would be an off-by-one that skips an event for ever, and the engine is idempotent per event, so a re-read costs a lookup. The owner-facing receipt therefore leads with `episodic_created`, which is exact.

red_first.the_scheduler_wiring: Three defects in the scheduler itself were found by its own tests before anything was committed: the exclusion the docstring claimed but the code did not apply, the cursor seeded from a horizon, and the graph reading its own receipt. Each was a real failing test first.
red_first.the_focus_resolution: `memory.forget` with no id and nothing read back must still refuse - proven by a test, because the convenience becoming a guess is the one way this could make `memory.forget` worse than B16 left it.

runtime_proof.why: REAL_PROOF_REQUIRED is at least one memory derived from activity IN PRODUCTION. Everything short of the production round is proven: real ledger events written through the real writer, read by the real engine on the real scheduler, becoming real memory rows; the scheduler bound to the routine clock on the real application object and reporting on /health. The remaining step is the production round, which is Karar 0.
